input: List three items a week on eBay for six months

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing what category of items will be listed determines how much sourcing, photography, and research work is involved — and whether a consistent supply of 72+ items is realistic.
Whether this is a solo effort or involves a partner/family member changes how tasks like photographing, shipping, and listing can be divided.
Understanding whether the user already has an eBay account and selling history affects the starting point — a new seller faces feedback, limits, and learning curve issues a veteran does not.
A hard time budget per week determines whether the plan is feasible and how much of the process needs to be streamlined or batched.
Knowing how items will be sourced — from existing possessions, thrifting, wholesale, etc. — defines the biggest operational bottleneck in sustaining the cadence.
The user's preferred listing format (auction vs. Buy It Now) and pricing strategy significantly affect how each listing is prepared and monitored.
Whether the goal is purely to hit the listing count, reach a revenue target, or clear out a specific inventory changes what 'done well' looks like at the end of six months.

gold.taskTitle: List 3 eBay items weekly for six months
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to consistently sell items on eBay by listing three new items every week for a six-month period.

questions.title: What type of items are you planning to sell?
questions.description: Identify the category or nature of items (e.g., secondhand clothing, collectibles, electronics, handmade goods) to determine sourcing complexity and listing effort.

questions.title: Do you already have an active eBay seller account?
questions.description: Establish whether the user is starting fresh or building on an existing account, which affects feedback standing, selling limits, and onboarding steps.

questions.title: Where will the items you list come from?
questions.description: Clarify the sourcing method — existing possessions, thrift stores, wholesale, dropshipping, etc. — since this is the primary constraint on sustaining a 72-item cadence.

questions.title: How many hours per week can you dedicate to this?
questions.description: Determine the weekly time budget to assess feasibility and decide how much batching or streamlining is needed across photography, listing, and shipping.

questions.title: Will you manage this alone or with someone helping you?
questions.description: Find out if another person is involved so tasks like packing, photographing, and scheduling can be allocated appropriately.

questions.title: Do you prefer auction-style listings or fixed Buy It Now prices?
questions.description: Identify the preferred listing format and pricing approach, which shapes how each listing is set up and how actively it needs to be monitored.

questions.title: What does success look like at the end of six months?
questions.description: Clarify the primary goal — hitting the listing count, earning a specific revenue amount, clearing a set inventory — so the plan can be oriented toward the right outcome.
